gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: patient presents with anxiety symptoms. Generated CC: anxiety that has worsened over the past two months. Core complaint of anxiety is captured; added detail about worsening is extra but not contradictory.
Gold: two‑month history of feeling anxious all the time. Generated HPI mentions daily morning anxiety/fear leaving house but not a two‑month duration or feeling anxious ‘all the time’.

Gold: anxiety began after starting new job in different industry with pressure from boss. Generated: onset with stressful new job in fashion retail; boss not supportive. Captures same causal relationship with additional detail (industry, non‑supportive boss).

Gold: dreads going to work every morning. Generated HPI‑001: daily morning anxiety and fear about leaving the house; HPI‑012: has not missed work but dreads attending. Combined, clearly cover dread of going to work every morning.

Gold: severe initial insomnia, ~3 hours to fall asleep. Generated HPI‑003: prolonged sleep onset, 3–4h/night, shallow sleep. Initial/prolonged sleep onset is captured; exact 3‑hour latency not specified but concept is covered.
Gold: early‑morning waking (EMW). Generated only notes prolonged sleep onset and short total sleep; EMW specifically is not described.
Gold: often only 3–4 hours sleep. Generated HPI‑003: 3–4h/night of shallow sleep. Directly matches.
Gold: tired during the day. Generated facts do not mention daytime tiredness/fatigue directly, only low energy and poor sleep.
Gold: low energy. Generated HPI‑004: reports low energy. Direct match.
Gold: eating pattern normal but more chocolate. Generated HPI‑013: no significant appetite change but more chocolate intake. Same content.

Gold: anhedonia at work and outside, still sees friends but often avoids; running/tennis/socialising. Generated HPI‑005 and HPI‑011: anhedonia, enjoys little day-to-day, difficulty with friends and running/tennis, increased social avoidance. Content is captured with similar examples.

Gold: palpitations began with anxiety symptoms. Generated HPI‑006: palpitations described but no explicit linkage to anxiety onset; however HPI‑007: no prior similar episodes of anxiety or palpitations implies they started with current episode, aligning with gold. Indirect but consistent coverage.
Gold: palpitations feel irregular and with chest discomfort. Generated HPI‑006: palpitations feel irregular, sometimes chest discomfort. Directly covered.
Gold: rapid palpitations lasting approx 2–10 minutes. Generated HPI‑006: few minutes–10 minutes; implies brief episodes. Does not state ‘rapid’ but rapidity is not contradicted; duration is covered.
Gold: has not missed work. Generated HPI‑012: has not missed work but dreads attending. Covered.
Gold: public transport is anxiety provoking. Generated HPI‑014: tube/public transport stressful but no avoidance of all public spaces. Matches and elaborates.
Gold: low mood most of the time. Generated HPI‑008: persistent low mood worsened by work. Persistent low mood = low most of the time; work‑related worsening is added detail.

Gold: no past psychiatric history/significant anxiety. Generated HPI‑007: no prior similar episodes of anxiety or palpitations; HPI‑015: no previous therapy. Together effectively capture lack of prior psych history/anxiety treatment.
Gold: mother has depression. Generated FH‑001: mother history of depression. Direct match.
Gold: lives with supportive parents. Generated SH‑001: lives with parents; SH‑005: good family support. Combined, this matches ‘supportive parents’.

Gold: drinks Fri/Sat, not sure of amount but sometimes overdoes it. Generated SH‑002: drinks above recommended limits on weekends and occasional midweek wine. Weekend pattern and excess use are captured; midweek wine is added detail.
Gold: smokes occasionally. Generated SH‑003: occasional smoker. Direct match.
Gold: no illicit drugs. Generated SH‑004: denies illicit drug use. Direct match.

Gold: work‑related anxiety. Generated ASM‑001: assessment includes work‑related anxiety triggered by stressful new occupation; details anticipatory anxiety, palpitations, etc. Core diagnosis is covered.
Gold: insomnia. Generated ASM‑002: secondary insomnia related to anxiety with poor initiation and reduced total sleep. Fully consistent.

Gold: advised self‑referral to NHS talking therapies. Generated PLAN‑001: refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT). Same intervention; generated implies provider‑initiated referral rather than self‑referral, which is extra but not clearly contradictory in content description.
Gold: advised to access online CBT resources, info attached. Generated PLAN‑002: provide online mental health resources. This encompasses online CBT resources.

Gold: advised blood test as initial investigation for palpitations, to book via support team. Generated PLAN‑004: arrange basic blood tests to rule out organic causes of palpitations. Core plan (blood tests for palpitations) is covered; booking via support team is omitted but minor.

Gold: contact clinic if anxiety/mood worse or unable to cope with work for further discussion. Generated PLAN‑006 / FU‑002: return if worsening anxiety, inability to cope, or deterioration in function. This includes work coping difficulty; covered.
Gold: no panic attacks. Generated facts do not mention panic attacks.
Gold: denies suicidal ideation (SI). Generated HPI‑010: denies SI; ASM‑001 also notes no self‑harm ideation. Covered.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold only notes anxiety symptoms as PC. Generated adds worsening over past 2 months, which is not specified in the chief complaint; duration appears in HPI but not as ‘worsened’. Thus this is an addition, though consistent.

No gold fact states specifically ‘daily morning anxiety and fear leaving house.’ Gold mentions dread going to work; fear leaving house and specifying daily morning anxiety is new detail not explicitly in gold.
Supported by gold onset with new job and pressure from boss, but generated adds specific industry (fashion retail) and that boss is not supportive—details not in gold.
Gold supports prolonged sleep onset and 3–4 hours sleep, but ‘shallow’ sleep is not stated in gold; that aspect is an addition.
Gold describes anhedonia in work and outside; generated summarises as anhedonia with little day‑to‑day enjoyment, consistent without extra specifics.

Gold: irregular palpitations with chest discomfort and duration 2–10 minutes and rapid beat. Generated adds they occur mainly in the morning and ‘sometimes’ chest discomfort. Morning predominance is additional detail; ‘sometimes’ chest discomfort slightly qualifies the gold but not a direct contradiction.
Gold: no past psych history/significant anxiety. Generated: no prior similar episodes of anxiety or palpitations. Consistent representation of no prior episodes.
Persistent low mood is supported by ‘low mood most of the time’; the specific statement that it is ‘worsened by work’ is not in gold and is added.
‘Enjoys little day to day’ restates global anhedonia; no extra conflicting detail.

Gold: previously enjoyed running, tennis, socialising; still sees friends but often avoids. Generated: difficulty engaging with friends and hobbies (running, tennis less frequent), increased social avoidance. All consistent but adds ‘less frequent’ and phrasing of ‘difficulty engaging’, which are interpretive expansions.
Gold: not missed work. Generated: has not missed work but dreads attending (supported by hpi‑003) and fears escalation of symptoms/work difficulties, which is extra anticipatory fear not in gold.
Gold: public transport anxiety provoking. Generated adds nuance: no avoidance of all public spaces; ‘tube/public transport stressful.’ The ‘no avoidance of all public spaces’ is new detail.
Gold mentions no previous psych history/significant anxiety but does not discuss prior therapy specifically, discussion with mother, or openness to 1:1 therapy. These are new psychosocial details.
Gold: drinks Fri/Sat, sometimes overdoes it. Generated: above recommended limits on weekends (consistent) and adds ‘occasional wine midweek’ which is not in gold.
‘Good family support’ rephrases ‘Lives with parents. Supportive.’
Gold facts provide no information about physical exam/vitals. Generated states that no findings are documented; this is a meta‑comment not derivable from gold facts alone.

Supported by gold work‑related anxiety, dread of work, palpitations, no work absence, and denied SI. However, ‘significant morning anticipatory anxiety,’ ‘functional impairment’ wording, and explicit consolidation of ‘no avoidance of work’ as part of the assessment add interpretive detail beyond gold.
Secondary insomnia with poor sleep initiation and reduced total sleep related to anxiety is fully consistent with gold HPI and assessment.

Gold: palpitations with chest discomfort (no qualifier that chest pain is absent). Generated: ‘no associated chest pain, rare chest discomfort.’ Introducing ‘no chest pain’ and ‘rare’ chest discomfort conflicts with gold’s unqualified mention of chest discomfort as an associated symptom.

Gold: advised self‑referral to NHS talking therapies. Generated: plan is to refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT). Mode of access differs (self‑referral vs clinician referral) and CBT specificity; CBT is supported by plan‑002 gold, but combining them as a single referral plan and changing self‑referral to referral is added/altered detail.
Online CBT resources are a subset of online mental health resources; statement is consistent and slightly more general but not contradictory.
Gold does not mention discussing sleep hygiene or providing such information; this is a new element of the care plan.
Ordering blood tests as initial investigation for palpitations implies ruling out organic causes; explicit rationale is added but consistent.

Gold plan only mentions that the patient should book blood tests via support team and when to contact the clinic if worse; it does not specify a GP follow‑up one week post‑bloods. This follow‑up timing is new.

Gold: contact us if anxiety/mood worse or unable to cope with work. Generated: return if worsening anxiety, inability to cope, or deterioration in function. Conceptually the same safety‑netting advice.

Gold follow‑up only says to contact if symptoms worsen or unable to cope with work; it does not state a scheduled GP follow‑up one week after blood tests. Thus this is an added specific follow‑up arrangement.
Restates the gold instruction to return if anxiety worsens or coping becomes difficult; ‘deterioration in function’ reasonably reflects being unable to cope with work.
